items.text: COMMITTEE DISCHARGED AND COMMITTED TO RULES

items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the family court act, in relation to expanding the right to
assistance of counsel to include petitioner kinship caregivers in custody and
guardianship proceedings and respondents in guardianship proceedings
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S6074

SPONSOR: SALAZAR
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the family court act, in relation to expanding the right
to assistance of counsel to include petitioner kinship caregivers in
custody and guardianship proceedings and respondents in guardianship
proceedings

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

To provide assigned counsel to indigent kinship caregivers in custody
and guardianship proceedings

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 amends subdivision (a) of section 262 of the family court act
to provide assigned counsel to kinship caregivers in custody and guardi-
anship proceedings.

Section 2 amends paragraph 1 of subdivision (a) of section 1094 of the
family court act to make a corresponding right to assignment of counsel
to kinship caregivers in Article 10 proceedings.

Section 3 is the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

When parents are unable to continue parenting due to unfortunate circum-
stances, New York often relies on kin to provide care for children.

Kinship caregivers are a valuable resource, keeping children in extended
families and out of foster care. This bill defines a kinship caregiver
as a person described in paragraph(a),(b)or(c)of subdivision 3 of
section 458-a of the social services law and acting as a parent of a
child.

Indigent kinship caregivers do not have a right to counsel when they
seek custody or guardianship in family court, and while some judges
occasionally assign counsel, many do not. Providing assignment of coun-
sel for indigent kinship caregivers will ensure that custody and guardi-
anship petitions are timely and fully considering the best interests of
children.

Additionally, New York's kinship guardian assistance program (KinGAP),
section 458a-f of the social services law, helps children to leave
foster care and to enter into the homes of kinship guardians. Under the
current law, financial assistance is provided to kinship guardians
during the petitioning process but not to indigent kinship guardians who
are subsequently, challenged.

Social justice impact: Incidents of neglect by biological parents, often
due to drug/alcohol abuse, are common reasons for children to live with
kinship caregivers. Ensuring that kinship caregivers can seek custody or
guardianship and that respondent guardians are provided counsel in fami-
ly court will provide for more balanced adjudications that produce the
best outcomes for children, without undermining parental rights.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

ASSEMBLY

A.7586 of 2019
05/10/19 referred to children and families
01/08/20 referred to children and families

SENATE

S.5434 of 2019
05/01/19 REFERRED TO JUDICIARY
01/08/20 REFERRED TO JUDICIARY

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS:

To be determined.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect on the first of April next succeeding the
date of which is shall have become law.
